summary: Iteration-5 (secret encryption at rest with cryptography.Fernet + 'enc:v1:' prefix) backend testing complete. Added /app/backend/tests/test_iteration5.py with 15 pytest cases covering: (1) POST /api/tenant-connections encrypts client_secret in Mongo (raw doc starts with 'enc:v1:'), masks response, reveal=true returns original plaintext ('plaintext-value-abc' round-trip verified); (2) PUT with empty client_secret keeps the exact same encrypted blob in Mongo (byte-for-byte identical) and reveal still returns original plaintext; (3) PUT with a new client_secret writes a DIFFERENT enc:v1: token and reveal returns the new value; (4) POST /tenant-connections/{id}/test decrypts secret before MSAL, returns ok=false with authority-config error, mode='live', no 500; (5) POST /api/projects encrypts BOTH source_tenant.client_secret and destination_tenant.client_secret in the raw Mongo doc; (6) GET /api/projects and GET /api/projects/{id} never include client_secret — each tenant object exposes has_secret bool (verified both in list and detail); (7) simulated-mode project (empty creds) discover returns mode='simulated' & 64 exchange items, test-connection returns simulated ok:true for both sides, preflight runs without crash, job with 3 items runs to completion with success_count>0; (8) backward compat: unit-level crypto.decrypt_secret returns legacy plaintext unchanged AND encrypt→decrypt round-trip yields original; a directly-inserted legacy Mongo doc with plaintext client_secret is served correctly by project GET (masked, has_secret=true) and test-connection responds 200. Regression: full suite is 86/86 (updated one iter4 assertion that expected pre-encryption behavior — project response leaking client_secret — to match new iter5 contract of has_secret:true). No backend 5xx caused by encryption path.

minor.issue: PRE-EXISTING (not iter5-caused): when a project has 'live-looking' but invalid tenant creds (e.g. fake tenant_id GUID), _discover propagates the MSAL ValueError as HTTP 500 instead of catching it like graph_adapter.test_connection does. Repro: create a project with fake tenant_id/client_id/client_secret, call discover — 500 with 'Unable to get authority configuration' in server logs. Suggest wrapping _discover's live branch in try/except and either falling back to simulated or surfacing a structured 4xx/200 with mode='live' + error. Affects any legacy plaintext record with fake creds too.

action_items: (Optional/minor) Wrap _discover live branch in try/except to convert MSAL ValueError into a structured response instead of 500. Not iter5-specific — pre-existing since live-graph discovery was introduced.
(Optional) Consider adding an audit_log entry when the /projects endpoint would previously have leaked client_secret, symmetric to the existing connection.reveal audit log.
critical_code_review_comments: crypto.py:47-52 — if CONN_ENCRYPTION_KEY is not set, encrypt_secret silently falls back to storing PLAINTEXT (only a WARNING log). In a production dev-fallback that's fine, but consider making this a hard error in a 'production' mode env flag (e.g. FAIL_IF_NO_ENC_KEY=true), otherwise a misconfigured deployment will silently store secrets in cleartext with no visible signal in API responses.

server.py:876-890 (_connection_out) — reveal=true returns the plaintext but the audit_log write (added in iter5, l.919-927) only fires from the get_tenant_connection endpoint. If any future code path calls _connection_out(doc, reveal=True) directly, it will bypass the audit trail. Recommend moving the audit_log insert INTO _connection_out (or a wrapper) so it's guaranteed on every reveal.

server.py:405-418 (_discover) — MSAL ValueError on live branch is not caught. See minor backend issue above. This surfaces as an HTTP 500 to the UI. Since decrypt_secret is called BEFORE the ValueError, the encryption path itself is safe, but user experience is poor. Suggested fix: wrap the DISCOVERY_MAP call in try/except and, on adapter/MSAL error, either return simulated items with a warning field, or return HTTP 200 with mode='live_error' + empty items + error message.

server.py:270-281 (_project_out) — has_secret is computed from stored value truthiness. If a legacy doc stores an empty string (""), has_secret=false; if it stores plaintext (any non-empty), has_secret=true. This works but consider also treating a value that CAN'T be decrypted as has_secret=false so a broken/corrupted enc token doesn't lie to the UI. Minor.
crypto.py:74-76 (is_encrypted) — trivial helper is fine; consider also exposing a `looks_valid` check that attempts decrypt but returns bool so callers can validate before running a job.
